name: Explore Confirm Separation Does Not Prove A Null Effect
text: Thibault and coauthors provide a methodological qualification to the registered null result. Their Explore and Confirm Analysis Workflow permits exploration on a data subset, but requires the resulting analysis script to be registered before access to the full dataset. The design preserves a confirmatory test on data not used to develop the analysis. That mechanism corresponds to Kaal's separation of the discovery run from confirmation. It does not establish that net discrimination was absent. It also does not recalculate the reported estimate or interval, examine Kaal's campaign units, or audit adherence to the preregistration. The external source supports the discovery-to-confirmation design logic only. Kaal's numerical result remains source-bound to the Article.

sourceProvenance.sourceProposition: Thibault and coauthors propose an Explore and Confirm Analysis Workflow in which researchers develop and register an analysis on a data subset before receiving the full dataset. The workflow preserves the confirmatory character of a final analysis while allowing the subset to support hypothesis generation and analysis development.

sourceEvidencePassages.text: The researchers then prepare an analysis script based on the subset of data, upload the analysis script to a registry, and then receive access to the full dataset.
Researchers may use the subset of data to generate hypotheses and/or to simply ensure that their intended analysis runs properly.
